reasoning: This is a centralized error notification workflow that activates when other workflows in the organization fail. The error trigger captures failed workflow executions and sends detailed error reports via Gmail to 'dlschoolautomations@gmail.com'. The email template includes workflow name, execution URL, error message, stack trace, and last executed node - providing comprehensive debugging information. With 40 executions and 85% success rate, this suggests the organization has experienced 40 workflow failures, with 6 instances where even the error notification itself failed. The 'FairTix Automations' project name and 'DL-School-Automations' email suggest this supports a ticketing platform's automation infrastructure. This workflow is critical infrastructure - it's the organization's primary mechanism for detecting and responding to automation failures across their entire suite of business processes.
name: Automation Failure Alert System
businessNarrative: This workflow serves as the organization's automation monitoring backbone, immediately notifying technical teams when any business-critical workflow fails. It provides comprehensive error diagnostics including stack traces and execution URLs, enabling rapid incident response for FairTix's automation infrastructure. The 40 recorded executions indicate significant automation activity, with the error notification system itself maintaining 85% reliability. This reveals an organization heavily dependent on automation for business operations, requiring robust failure detection to prevent silent business process breakdowns.
trigger: Any workflow failure across the FairTix automation platform
dataFlow: Receives workflow failure data (name, error details, execution context) and transforms it into structured email alerts sent to the automation operations team.
